main_text.p: cicadâ. Transiuit igitur à Boreali parte Sol, abiit autumnal, & hyems defcenditin terram. mare vé- rò tranquillitatis fuæ fidem fregit. nautæ portus, vt in quibus falui forent, funt amplexi, & rufticus fe ad suum recepit focum, ac formica in imis terræ vifceribus exiis, quæ laborauerat, pabulum habe- bat sufficiens. supplex verò cicada à formica petiit, vt partem sibi daret repositorum. hæc verò melo- dam ablegauit à suis foribus, irrifam valdè ob pi- gritiam: eis; in memoriam reuocauit æstiuos can- tus. Quapropter illi cessit cantus in famem: huic verò labor in luxum & opimitatem. Quadratin te fabula, Lysistrate. piger enim febricitante estinfe- licior, duplo tantum comedens, quantum diligens. apage igitur pigritiam, optime, confpurcasti enim naturæ dona, dum vires eiusmodi roburque cor- poris, laborum exercitio neglecto, incultum præ- teris.
main_text.head: Ruff. Tertigon Porphyrioni. LXII.
main_text.p: Felix vir est Corydon, & vt videtur, fortunæ amicus. Vites vuis grauantur, pyri curuantur, ac decerpi volunt, oleæ pronutantin terram, & mul- titudine fructuum ramos cogunt. prata, spissa græ- mine area florentibus similis sulcis. & muliercula post omnia exhilarat coniugem. Tot enim habet pueros, vt Danaum & Ægyptum fœcunditate vin- cat, alius enim est subrumus; alius lactare destitit; alij verò repunt nondum rectâ inambulantes: ali- qui balbutiunt, & dentes mutant: alij ad florem ve- niunt, & iam sunt adulti. arundinum in modum, quæ difpares collocantur in sistula, ætatum illi or- do con-

page.notes: Head "Ruff. Tertigon Porphyrioni. LXII." is uncertain: the Greek-derived word after "Tertigon" is hard to read at this scan resolution, and the Greek-style "Porphyrioni" was transcribed as printed. "Vites" and "Lysistrate" are readable but unverified. The paragraph ending "do con-" is cut at the foot of the scan; the continuation is not on this page. The left edge shows show-through from the neighbouring page and is excluded.
